dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi there! I submitted a home purchase loan application and wanted to check on the status — has a decision been made yet? I applied for an FHA loan for $595,000 with a 30-year term.
dialogue.agent:
Yes, a decision has been made on your application. Your loan was originated, meaning it was approved and finalized. Congratulations!

Is there anything else about the loan you'd like to know?

dialogue.user: Oh, that's great news! Thank you for letting me know. Could you tell me what interest rate I was approved for and what the total loan costs are? Also, what exactly is my loan term — I want to make sure it’s the 30 years I requested.
dialogue.agent:
Certainly. Your interest rate is 5.75%, and your total loan costs are $22,778.16. Your loan term is 360 months, which is exactly 30 years as requested.

Is there anything else you’d like to ask?

dialogue.user:
5.75% and $22,000 in costs — okay, that's helpful to know. I appreciate that. 

Just a couple more questions: Are there any high-cost or negative amortization flags on my loan? And has my loan been sold or transferred to another institution?
dialogue.agent:
Your loan is not classified as a high-cost mortgage under HOEPA, and there is no negative amortization feature. 

Regarding the sale of your loan, it was sold to a credit union, mortgage company, or finance company.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?

dialogue.user:
Okay, I'm relieved about the no high-cost and no negative amortization part. 

But hold on — you're saying my loan was sold to another institution? I wasn't aware of that. When did that happen? And does that change anything about my rate or terms I originally agreed to?
dialogue.agent:
I understand your concern. I can confirm from the record that the loan was sold, but I don’t have any specific sale date or details about the timing.

As for how it affects your rate and terms, my records don’t include information on changes after the loan was originated. I’m only able to provide what’s in the application record itself, which shows your original terms as we discussed.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

dialogue.user:
That's a bit unsettling to hear the loan was sold without knowing exactly when or to whom, but I understand you can only tell me what's in the record. 

One last thing — what does my debt-to-income ratio look like for this loan? I'm curious how it played into the approval.
dialogue.agent:
Your debt-to-income ratio was 49%. This means your total monthly debts, including the proposed housing payment, made up 49% of your monthly income. 

The record doesn't include specific underwriting rationale on how this affected the approval decision, only that the loan was originated.

I've shared everything I have from your loan record. I hope this information helps. Take care.

Thanks for all the details. I appreciate you taking the time to walk through everything with me. I have enough information now.
